newsitem.title: FRANCE: French group-Jordanian Airline sign Airbus leases.
newsitem.headline: French group-Jordanian Airline sign Airbus leases.

text.p: Aircraft Development Company (ADC), a French aerospace and defence consortium, and its United Arab Emirates' (UAE) partners signed on Thursday a $134 million agreement with Royal Jordanian Airline for refinancing and lease of four Airbus A310 jets.
French defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF, aerospace group Aerospatiale and arms maker Giat Industries created ADC to meet offset requirements arising from the sale of their equipment to the UAE.
Aerospatiale, Thomson-CSF, Giat, and Indosuez Air Finance invested a total $23 million in the lease agreement.
The firms set up ADC to "develop leasing activities related to the aerospace industry," a Thomson-CSF official said on the margins of the signing ceremony at the Paris air show.
The UAE requires 60 percent of contract values to be reinvested through the local economy, he said.
ADC will look for investment opportunities for UAE investors and harness the ample finances in the region, he said.
The lease agreement is backed by export credit agencies of France, Britain and Germany and commercial banks, Credit Lyonnais and BNP, Thomson-CSF said in a statement.

Credit Lyonnais is the lead for a consortium of 37 European banks for the export credit financing share of the lease agreement, with Midland Bank, a HongKong Shanghai Corp unit, acting as lead manager in Britain, and Dresdner Bank (desk pls check rix) in Germany.
BNP is leading a bank consortium for the commercial credit portion.

Airbus Industrie is a consortium made up of French state-owned Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
